title: Revisit what SL-088 went ahead with: At Hidden=2, 0 of 13 hidden/system reveals selected the item; control passed 4/4
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: Derived C1: before a reveal, the app reads Explorer's hidden-item settings with SHGetSetSettings(SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN) and never writes them: missing
Derived C2: when hidden files are not shown (Hidden=2 / fShowAllObjects=false), a reveal of a Hidden-only item that opens S_OK is reported as parent-only, not as landing on the item: missing
Derived C3: when protected OS files are not shown (ShowSuperHidden=0), a Hidden+System item is reported as parent-only (SC-120's promise), whichever settings are in force: missing
Derived C4: the status line says so, telling the user that Explorer opened the parent without selecting the item, and only when the settings in force mean that is what happened: missing

Claimed measurement: at Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0, 0 of 13 Hidden and Hidden+System reveals selected the item, with the parent opened each time and no dialog or elevation; the non-hidden control landed 4 of 4: unknown

The status text is composed in App code-behind (FormatRevealStatus), so its three label variants are checked only through R-003 window runs. Moving the text into Core would make them checkable by xUnit, but would split UI wording from the window.
The tests/window rule is settled rather than twinned. A twin would let dotnet test catch a settings write in a window script during build, at the cost of a Fact and parity-count churn.

The refusal is not a KnownWorkarounds entry, on the reading that Explorer obeying its own view setting is not a defect. A reviewer who reads S_OK-with-nothing-selected as an outside defect would want a checkbox, but its 'off' position could only restore this project's own false report.
Wording: "Explorer hides '<leaf>' (<label>)" versus "Explorer's settings hide '<leaf>'". The proposal's form keeps the leaf earlier on a line that gets cut.
One NoWrap ellipsis line with a tooltip, rather than a status line that wraps.

R-001 and R-002 were not run: their steps open real Explorer windows and are person-run (Q-176 covered SL-089 only). R-001 step 5 is updated to the derived expectation but has not been executed through this build.

The Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0 sitting (0/13 re-measurement through the exe, the host ancestor harness on 26200, WindowsApps, System-only items), the (1,1)/(2,1) cells, the mid-session toggle, and the Windows 10 check all need a person to change Explorer's settings or use another machine. They are filed in the design note.
The architecture record edit for C-004 is proposed in `architecture`, not applied: no stage can write the record (Q-125).

WindowCases.ps1 Invoke-Sized returns the output of CheckActed, CheckSized, CheckDrives and CheckStatusShown along with its result, so S-001..S-008 never print those check lines. Failures are still counted. This was already the case before SL-091.

B-008 fails 'the outcome's title and detail run longer than a system drive's' (384 against 400 characters) when TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, as in the engine's sessions: the root is 18 characters shorter than under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, where it passes. The case should pad its root to a fixed length, as R-001 does.
Rule A could also name SHGetSettings, the older read-only reader of the same shell state, which attempt 1's rule had.
WindowMutants.ps1 still hard-codes the -Mutant All roster beside the ValidateSet. Q-115's startup check that the two agree is not built, so every new mutant has to be added twice.
docs/design/SL-088-reveal-lands-or-refuses.md still describes the old hidden note and the H+S gap as SL-088 shipped them. SL-091's note supersedes it, but nothing in that file points there.

deviation: Rule B (src) is wider than the design and n2 asked, to close the class (O-044): (?i) on the SetValue pattern because registry value names are not case-sensitive; @? for verbatim strings; (?i) and ReadWriteSubTree on the OpenSubKey pattern, which attempt 1 caught; and the RegSetValue pattern widened to RegSetKeyValue, SHSetValue and SHRegSetUSValue. Every pattern stays single-line, and the corpus rows pin each widening.

deviation: Rule C (tests/window) is wider than the design: Remove/Clear-ItemProperty, reg delete, (?i) on the shell call (PowerShell writes $True), SetValue in either quote, writable OpenSubKey and CreateSubKey, and the RegSetValue family, beside n2's -Name and ::SetValue patterns. The design's 'path held in a variable is not caught' no longer holds when -Name names Hidden or ShowSuperHidden; the known misses left are pinned in the corpus.

deviation: Attempt 1's settled rule 'the Core tests never change the person's Explorer settings' (tests/**/*.cs) is not carried over: this design did not declare it, and n1 said to delete the attempt-1 block whole. The Core tests only read HKCU.

deviation: R-001 step 5 also reveals a new Hidden-only h_file.dat with the derived expectation. Without it, the design's filed person item ('an H-only reveal at (1,0) lands with an empty status line') had no step to run.

deviation: R-003 step (b) targets the Hidden+System file, which the design left unspecified. If the hook ever failed to arm, the reveal would still be refused under any settings but (1,1), so nothing opens on this PC.

deviation: CheckStatusShown gained one assertion beyond n4's logging: the refusal's lead ("Nothing was opened: Explorer hides '") must show before the ellipsis. It turns m1's ordering into something a run checks.
deviation: The Folder Options label for protected files is used without the dialog's '(Recommended)' suffix (design wording). The full resolved strings are recorded in the design note.
deviation: Walk's open-failure outcome now carries the Hidden/System attributes and the View it read, where it used to carry false/false. The reason and HRESULT are unchanged.
deviation: ExplorerView is a sealed record class, not a struct, so the override can be published with Volatile.Write/Read as the design requires.
deviation: No release-notes or known-limits list exists in this repository, so Q-197's Windows 10 limit is recorded only in docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md.

drift: The twinned rules A and B are in .taad/fitness.yaml:267-286 under Fact-style names, 'OnlyShellRevealReadsOrOverridesExplorersViewSettings (*.cs)' and 'TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings (*.cs)'. The design declared them as 'only ShellReveal.cs reads or overrides Explorer's view settings' and 'the app never writes Explorer's settings'. The yaml comment and the design note explain the twinning, but the rename is not in the declared deviations. Review n1 recorded the engine appending declared rules only when no entry of that name exists. If the engine reconciles this design's architecture_rules by name again, it would find A and B absent. It would then append settled copies, which would STRAY-HIT plants F41-F48 and change the settled count (63).

drift: Nothing else departs undeclared. The other departures I found (wider rule B and rule C patterns, R-001's added h_file.dat, R-003(b)'s H+S target, the extra CheckStatusShown assertion, the label without '(Recommended)', Hidden/System/View on the open-failure outcome, ExplorerView as a record class, the Windows 10 limit kept only in the design note) are all in the build's deviations list.

not reached: What Explorer actually selects at Windows' defaults (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0). The 0-of-13 claim behind this slice was not re-measured: it needs a person to change the setting, and the exe now refuses before any open (SC-159).

not reached: O-041: whether Explorer's own Apply or View toggle clears shell32's cached view in a running app. Only a raw change to the underlying values has been observed, and it went unseen for at least 3.8 s.
not reached: R-001 step 5 and R-002 through the exe: an H-only item at this PC's (1,0) landing selected, with an empty status line. These open real Explorer windows.
not reached: The H+S landing at (1,1) in Explorer itself. The app's Exact decision was measured with the live shell reading 0x8001 from a private hive; Explorer's selection was not.

not reached: What SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems does with the ID list of an item deleted between the parse and the attribute read. Criterion 14's probe faked the open; by design the reveal goes to the open and reports what the open returns.
not reached: A hidden folder above the item not blocking selection on this host's build 26200 at Hidden=2. It was measured only in Windows Sandbox (26100) and through the run-2285 control.
not reached: The real C:\Program Files\WindowsApps, and real System-only items, at Windows' defaults.
not reached: Windows 10: the SHGetSetSettings decode and Explorer's hidden-item filtering (Q-197, Q-199).

critique missed: The design's person sitting and its harness reuse could not do what they said. filed_for_later item 1 had the owner 're-measure 0/13 through the shipped exe', and 'whats_reused' named the spike-92 harness, which compiles the live ShellReveal.cs. The same design's gate refuses every hidden target before the open, so neither could observe Explorer's selection. The check was missing: for each filed measurement, name the code path that still reaches SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems after the gate. Four critique passes did not ask it.

critique missed: The design's Walk contract lists 'An open failure after a visible verdict gives Failed / None with that hr', but its 14-row case matrix has no row for it. The only open-failure test walks the never-created C:\a\b.txt, so its attribute read throws and the Hidden-visible open-failure branch is never reached. The build then changed what that branch carries (Hidden, System and View), and a regression there would have stayed green. Every error_case in a contract needs a case row or an explicit 'immaterial' entry.

critique missed: The design listed mid-session freshness of SHGetSetSettings both as a cross-domain invariant marked 'must-verify' and as a filed person item. The invariant became validate-aimed obligation O-041, which needs a person to toggle Explorer's settings. The critique did not force a single owner for it, so validate ran three laps on an obligation it could not discharge.

still unknown: Does shell32's cached SHGetSetSettings in a running app refresh after Explorer's own Apply or a View toggle (O-041, SC-162)? Attempt 2 saw a raw registry change go unseen for at least 3.8 s. If it is stale, the app refuses items Explorer would now show, or reports landings it will not make, until restart.

still unknown: At (Hidden=1, ShowSuperHidden=1), does Explorer select a Hidden+System item on the host (26200, Medium-integrity Explorer)? The predicate returns Exact there. Only the SHGetSetSettings decode was measured, through a private hive. Explorer's selection was not. This is the only cell where the predicate claims Exact without a measurement.

still unknown: Do +H direct-parent and +H+S ancestor rows hold on the host (build 26200, Medium-integrity Explorer) at Hidden=2? Evidence so far is Sandbox build 26100 with a High-integrity Explorer (18/18 per class) plus run 2285's control under +H AppData four levels up.

still unknown: Can a Windows Sandbox guest's Explorer be switched between settings cells unattended (guest HKCU write plus a shell-state broadcast, or UI automation) so that its running Explorer actually follows the change? That decides whether the candidate below can replace the owner's sitting.
still unknown: Windows 10: does SHGetSetSettings decode bit 0 and bit 15 the same way, and does Explorer filter hidden items the same way (Q-197, Q-199)? Nothing has been measured there.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-017: unsettled design fork: At Windows defaults (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0), does a Hidden or Hidden+System ancestor stop Explorer selecting a non-hidden item inside it? Examples: AppData\Local, ProgramData\Microsoft, files under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Its context: - This design assumes only the item's own attributes matter. It was measured 13/13 at Hidden=1 only. - The alternative: Walk reads every ancestor's attributes, and the refusal names the hidden ancestor instead of the leaf. Spike 'hidden-ancestor-does-not-block-selection-at-defaults' has a harness ready. It needs a person to set 'Don't show hidden files' and run it. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Send this fork back to the risk spike to be measured. The question is whether a hidden ancestor blocks selection at Windows defaults, and the measurement decides it. Steps, in order: 1. Read what is already on the machine before asking anyone. The engine record for the person's hand run (run 2285, 2026-09-29T16:23Z) holds the full log. The brief cuts it off. Look for the full path of short/ctrl_dir and long/ctrl_dir and the attributes of every folder above them. If the 62-character ctrl_dir sat under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (inside AppData, which is Hidden only) and landed with selOk=True and folderOk=True while the gate read Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0, that settles the Hidden-ancestor half. It does not settle the Hidden+System-ancestor half. Record the result either way. Do not take this inference from path lengths as the answer by itself. 2. Ask the person for one sitting with the prepared harness 'hidden-ancestor-does-not-block-selection-at-defaults' (bin\h.dll through run.ps1, then verify.ps1). It runs the real ShellReveal unchanged on .NET 10 from the repo's .dotnet. The steps are: - close every Explorer window, because the harness aborts if one is open; - set File Explorer Options > View > 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives', keeping 'Hide protected operating system files' on (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0); - run run.ps1 without --dry; - set 'Show hidden files' back (Hidden=1); - run verify.ps1 and confirm Hidden=1 / ShowSuperHidden=0 in both the registry and SHGetSetSettings. Cases to cover: - C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local; - C:\ProgramData\Microsoft; - a plain file and folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp; - a plain file and folder directly inside a +H temp folder and inside a +H+S temp folder, at about 88 characters and at more than 260 characters; - the hidden-file-inside-a-hidden-folder case; - the D:\ controls. Every case logs the target's own attributes and each hidden ancestor. In the same Hidden=2 sitting, also run the already-filed Hidden=2 re-measurement through the shipped exe (the 0/13 rerun plus C:\Program Files\WindowsApps, and System-only items), logging each control's full path and ancestor attributes. One settings change then covers both. 3. How the result decides the fork. The run is void if the settings gate does not read Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0, or if the D:\ control does not land. - Own attributes only (the current design stands, no change to Walk, contracts or data model): every non-hidden item under a Hidden or Hidden+System ancestor is selected in its own parent within 5 s, with the leaf name matched (or the GetLongPathName-resolved alias), the right parent folder, no #32770 dialog and no consent.exe. - Design rewritten with an ancestor walk: any such item ends with an empty SelectedItems(), a different leaf, or a different window folder. Walk then reads attributes from the target's parent up to the volume root, not including the root, which stays exempt. It applies the same predicate to each ancestor: Hidden && !ShowsHidden gives HiddenFiles; Hidden && System && !ShowsProtected gives ProtectedFiles. It refuses with nothing opened, and RevealOutcome and the status line name the nearest hiding ancestor as well as the setting. - If only one ancestor class blocks (for example +H+S blocks and +H does not), the ancestor rule covers only that class. The predicate table gets the matching row. - The hidden-file-inside-a-hidden-folder case must open that hidden folder with nothing selected. If it opens anything else, record it as a separate fact for the predicate table. Nothing has measured this. The only data is 13/13 at Hidden=1, where hidden ancestors are visible anyway, so it says nothing about defaults. Both positions are possible outcomes of one run that nobody has made, and a harness for it is already built and tested. Guessing is expensive here. If the answer is wrong one way, every reveal under AppData or ProgramData at Windows defaults reports a false Exact, which is the false success this slice exists to remove. If it is wrong the other way, Walk, RevealOutcome and the status-line contract gain an ancestor walk nobody needs. The synthesis flagged that either loss forces a re-synthesis. The brief does not fix this question, and no person has decided it. Q-175 left the predicate to measurement. So it is not a reason to escalate. Making the decision by building is ruled out too. No engine stage may change Explorer's Hidden setting, so the run needs the person. That is why step 1 reads what is already on the machine first, to keep the person's sitting short. The measure budget is unused (0 of 2 laps). Doing this in the same sitting as the already-filed Hidden=2 re-measurement means the person changes the setting only once. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
